Build a cPanel/Plesk-style CONTROL PANEL into the Nxeon customer server-management page in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Prisma + PostgreSQL, tsx worker daemon). It manages the customer's own VPS over SSH. The user approved ALL FOUR capability bundles; build them as a cohesive set of new tabs on the server detail page, **fully consistent with the Nxeon dark navy/violet theme** (reuse the existing `card`/`btn-primary`/`btn-secondary`/`btn-ghost`/`input`/`label`/`section-label`/`glass` classes and the `ServerTabs` tab pattern already on that page — it must NOT look like a bolted-on cPanel).

## The four bundles
1. **Websites & PHP** — add a website: domain → generate an nginx server block (doc root under `/var/www/<domain>`), pick PHP version (install php-fpm if needed), enable/disable, one-click Let's Encrypt SSL (certbot), and subdomains. List/edit/delete sites.
2. **Databases** — create/list/delete MySQL/MariaDB & PostgreSQL databases and DB users on the VPS, with generated passwords shown once. (Install the engine on first use.)
3. **One-click apps** — install WordPress / Ghost / Nextcloud (+a couple more) onto the server: provision a site (vhost+docroot) + a database + the app, report the URL/admin creds. Reuse the Websites + Databases primitives.
4. **Cron jobs & services** — add/edit/remove cron entries; start/stop/restart common services (nginx, php-fpm, mysql, docker…); a live process/resource snapshot (top processes, CPU/RAM/disk).

## Study & reuse first (do NOT run git or `npm run build`)
- How the codebase already runs SSH work on a customer server: `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `terminal-server/`, `worker/game-update.ts` (ssh2 usage + how root creds are obtained: `serverRootPassword`/`rootPasswordEnc`). Reuse or factor a shared **injection-safe SSH-exec helper** (validate every interpolated value against a strict shell-inert allowlist; secrets via file/STDIN never argv; timeouts) — mirror the hardening in `worker/migrate-real.ts`. Do NOT weaken those patterns.
- `lib/sandbox.ts` (`SANDBOX`) — in the sandbox (staging) every real SSH action must be SIMULATED with realistic synthetic results (no real commands), exactly like the other worker features. Real execution only on prod (non-sandbox).
- `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` + `components/customer/ServerTabs.tsx` — how tabs are declared/rendered; add the new tabs here (a grouped "Control panel" or individual tabs — your call, but keep the page readable). NOTE another agent is concurrently editing `components/customer/MigrationWizard.tsx`, `worker/migrate*.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts` and the migrate route — do NOT touch those files.
- The worker job dispatcher (`worker/index.ts` + how `Job` kinds are handled) — register any new job kinds you add.

## YOU OWN prisma/schema.prisma this wave
Add the models you need (e.g. `Website`, `VpsDatabase`, `CronJob` — each scoped to a `Server`/`userId`, with status + timestamps). After editing the schema, run `npx prisma generate` (LOCAL client generation only — safe, no DB). Do NOT run `npx prisma db push` or `db:seed` (the parent applies the schema to the real DBs during integration). Keep migrations non-destructive/additive.

## Architecture
- Server actions in new files (e.g. `lib/actions-websites.ts`, `lib/actions-databases.ts`, `lib/actions-apps.ts`, `lib/actions-cron.ts`), all `"use server"`, each op: `requireUser()` + server-ownership check + rate-limit + the "one in-flight job per server" respect where a job is queued. Real work runs in worker executors (new `worker/*.ts`) over SSH, sandbox-gated. Quick reads (list sites/dbs/cron, service status, process snapshot) can run inline with a short SSH timeout, also sandbox-synthetic.
- UI components under `components/customer/cpanel/` (or similar), themed. Loading/empty/error states everywhere. Generated passwords shown once with a copy button. Destructive actions confirm.
- Remember a `"use server"` file may only export async functions — put any shared const/type in a plain module.

## Constraints
- No new npm deps. Do NOT touch the migration/resize/terminal/email files listed above. Do NOT run git or `npm run build` or `prisma db push`.
- Write/Edit may time out on a hook — fall back to Bash heredocs and verify files exist.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate >/dev/null 2>&1; npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (must be clean for your files).
- Build a real, coherent v1. If time forces a trade-off, prioritize a solid shared SSH foundation + Databases + Cron/Services fully working, then Websites & PHP, then One-click apps — and clearly report what is fully wired vs simplified/stubbed.

Report: new schema models, the shared SSH-exec helper + how it stays injection-safe, each bundle's actions + worker executors + UI tabs, how SANDBOX simulates them, new job kinds registered, and the done-vs-stubbed status of each of the four bundles.

## Report: cPanel/Plesk-style Control Panel for Nxeon

Built a cohesive **Control panel** as a single new main tab on the server detail page (`/dashboard/servers/[id]`), with four inner sub-tabs. It reuses the existing `card`/`btn-*`/`input`/`label`/`section-label`/`glass`/`table-shell` classes and the `ServerTabs` pattern, so it reads as native Nxeon, not a bolted-on cPanel.

### New schema models (`prisma/schema.prisma` — owned this wave)
- **`Website`** — domain, docRoot, phpVersion, ssl, enabled, isSubdomain/parentDomain, appSlug, status, error; `@@unique([serverId, domain])`, cascade on server.
- **`VpsDatabase`** — engine, name, dbUser, `passwordEnc` (transient), status; `@@unique([serverId, engine, name])`.
- **`AppInstall`** — appSlug, domain, websiteId/databaseId, url, adminUser, `adminPassEnc` (transient), status.
- **`CronJob`** — schedule, command, comment, enabled, status.
- All scoped to `Server` + `userId`, with timestamps and `onDelete: Cascade`. Added back-relations on `Server`. `npx prisma generate` run (no `db push`). **9 new `JobType` enum values** registered.

### Shared SSH-exec foundation (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`, plain server module)
Factored the injection-safe helper mirroring `worker/migrate-real.ts`:
- **Strict allowlist validators** (`DOMAIN_RE`, `IDENT_RE`, `PHP_VERSION_RE`, `SERVICE_RE`, `PATH_RE`, `CRON_FIELD_RE`, `SLUG_RE`) with `assert*` helpers that **reject, never sanitize** — every charset is shell-inert.
- **Secrets never touch argv**: `execInput()` streams generated DB/app passwords into the remote command's STDIN (SQL body / `cat > wp-config.php` / `crontab -`); command strings reference only validated values/paths. Defensive `shellQuote` on top.
- `withServerSsh` (connect via `connectionTarget`+`serverRootPassword` exactly like `lib/sftp`, always closes), `exec`/`execInput` with per-command timeouts, `pkgInstallPrefix`, `generateStrongPassword`.
- Client-safe consts/types split into `lib/cpanel-types.ts` (imports nothing) so the UI and `"use server"` files can share them.

### The four bundles
Each has a `"use server"` actions file (all ops: `requireUser()` + ownership check + per-user rate-limit + reject when a lifecycle/destructive job is in flight + `RUNNING` guard), worker executors, and a themed panel with loading/empty/error states.

1. **Websites & PHP** — `lib/actions-websites.ts` + `worker/websites.ts` (`WEBSITE_CREATE/DELETE/TOGGLE/SSL`). Generates an nginx server block (docroot `/var/www/<domain>`), installs php-fpm + extensions on demand, enable/disable via sites-enabled symlink, one-click certbot `--nginx` SSL, subdomains. **Fully wired.**
2. **Databases** — `lib/actions-databases.ts` + `worker/databases.ts` (`DB_CREATE/DELETE`). MySQL/MariaDB & PostgreSQL DB+user creation (engine installed on first use), password **generated + shown once** via a `SecretCard` with copy, stored encrypted only transiently and scrubbed after apply. **Fully wired.**
3. **One-click apps** — `lib/actions-apps.ts` + `worker/apps.ts` (`APP_INSTALL`). Reuses the Website+Database primitives (WordPress, Ghost, Nextcloud, Joomla, Matomo). Real WordPress is installed end-to-end (core download + `wp-config.php`); the other apps get vhost+DB provisioned + landing page, marked ready — **runtime setup of the non-PHP app (Ghost) is intentionally left to the customer** (the honest simplification). Creds shown once.
4. **Cron & Services** — `lib/actions-cron.ts` + `worker/services.ts` (`CRON_SYNC`, `SERVICE_ACTION`). Cron add/toggle/delete (rebuilt into one managed crontab block via STDIN; `updateCronJob` action also exported), start/stop/restart of nginx/mysql/postgres/php-fpm/docker/redis/ssh, live service status + auto-refreshing process/resource snapshot (top procs, CPU/RAM/disk/load/uptime). **Fully wired** (inline reads served via `lib/cpanel-inline.ts`).

### SANDBOX behavior
Every real SSH action is gated. Inline reads (`lib/cpanel-inline.ts`) return **deterministic synthetic** service statuses and a realistic process snapshot in sandbox — no SSH opened. Worker executors, in sandbox, flip DB-row statuses to `ACTIVE`/`DISABLED` with synthetic success + notifications and scrub secrets, exactly like `worker/ssl.ts`/`volumes.ts`. Real execution additionally requires `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL=1` on prod (belt-and-suspenders mirroring `ENABLE_REAL_SSL`), so a fresh prod box isn't mutated until an operator opts in — **noted as a deliberate choice**; flip the default if you want real work on any non-sandbox box.

### Files touched (allowed only)
`prisma/schema.prisma`, `worker/index.ts` (imports + handlers map), `components/customer/ServerTabs.tsx` (added tab + prop), `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` (mounts `<ControlPanel>`). New: 3 `lib/*` shared modules, 4 `lib/actions-*.ts`, 4 `worker/*.ts`, 6 `components/customer/cpanel/*.tsx`.

### Done vs simplified
- **Fully wired:** shared SSH foundation, Databases, Cron & Services, Websites & PHP.
- **Simplified (clearly):** one-click apps install WordPress fully on the real path; other catalog apps provision site+DB+landing page (runtime finish left to the user). Cron *edit* exists as a server action but the UI exposes add/pause/delete (edit = delete+recreate). SSL for standalone Website rows uses certbot `--nginx`; it coexists with the pre-existing `SslCertificate` flow rather than merging with it.
